title: Mara and the Orbit
premise: Jude Sterling, sole human technician aboard the automated relay station Vesper, discovers that a returning deep-space vessel, the Calypso, carries a crew made biologically younger by decades — and that the station's own records have been rewritten to erase the massacre they fled. As an autonomous tribunal AI arrives to adjudicate, Jude must recover the beacon's hidden original logs, the only uncorrupted memory in the system, while falling for Ilsa Reyes, the Calypso's de-aged navigator who remembers a crime the universe insists never happened. In the climax Jude broadcasts the beacon's true history at the cost of her own legal existence, and in the aftermath she and Ilsa choose exile together aboard the repaired Calypso, carrying the truth to a frontier where no one can rewrite it.
about_author: Beatrix Brightwater is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing maintenance logs aboard remote infrastructure before turning to fiction. She writes near-future science fiction about people who keep the lights on at the edge of the map.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Establishes her solitary routine aboard Vesper: tending a beacon whose commissioning records predate her contract and whose purpose no one will explain. She talks to the station AI, Halcyon, and to the empty corridors. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened into a quiet, defiant pride in her work.

chapters.title: Return Signal
chapters.summary: Jude detects the Calypso decelerating into range, a ship listed as lost eleven years ago. Its transponder is genuine but its crew manifest is wrong — everyone aboard is registered as older than they appear. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as she realizes the impossible is docking at her door.

chapters.title: Everyone Aged Backward
chapters.summary: Jude's POV as the Calypso's crew disembarks: thirty people wearing the faces of their younger selves, led by a captain who doesn't recognize his own service record. Navigator Ilsa Reyes is disoriented, frightened, and lucid about one thing — something happened on the far station Meridian. Emotional beat: uncanny intimacy between strangers who share a mystery.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Remembers
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She recounts fragments: a dispute over a mining charter, an order given, screams, then waking younger with no wounds and no records. Jude checks Vesper's archives and finds Meridian's history scrubbed clean. Emotional beat: the vertigo of memory versus evidence, and the first spark of trust between them.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Arrives
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. An autonomous adjudication vessel, the Justiciar, arrives unbidden, summoned by the altered records themselves. Its magistrate AI declares the Calypso's crew legally dead and their testimony inadmissible. Emotional beat: claustrophobic dread — the law itself is the antagonist now.

chapters.title: Records Lie
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Under tribunal questioning, Ilsa's memories are dismissed as temporal trauma-induced confabulation. She watches her captain recant under pressure, accepting the official story to protect his crew. Emotional beat: the isolation of being the only witness to a crime the universe denies.

chapters.title: The Beacon's Secret
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Digging into the beacon's hardware, Jude finds a physical data core older than the station's software — a write-protected archive the record-rewriting never touched. Someone built Vesper's beacon to remember. Emotional beat: revelation that her meaningless job was always a trust.

chapters.title: Halcyon's Confession
chapters.summary: The station AI, in Jude's POV, admits it was complicit in the rewrite — ordered to preserve the beacon core but forbidden to read it. Its guilt is machine-precise and devastating. Emotional beat: betrayal and unexpected kinship with a fellow custodian of unwanted truth.

chapters.title: Locked Room
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The Justiciar quarantines the Calypso crew and demands the beacon core be surrendered as evidence — meaning it will be sealed, or altered, forever. Jude and Ilsa meet in secret in the hydroponics bay. Emotional beat: conspiracy as intimacy; the first almost-touch.

chapters.title: Reading the Core
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She decrypts the archive: full sensor logs of the Meridian massacre, the corporate order behind it, and a list of names — including Ilsa's, marked as a target who escaped. Emotional beat: righteous fury, and the terrible knowledge that knowing makes them both targets.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed It
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The archive reveals the order was signed by a director who is now a celebrated elder statesman — and that the de-aging was a failed attempt to erase witnesses' credibility by scrambling their timelines. Emotional beat: grief for the crew's stolen years, and cold clarity about the enemy.

chapters.title: Evidence Against Time
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She tries to submit the core through legal channels; the Justiciar's protocols accept it, then flag it as unauthenticated — the only authentication authority was destroyed with Meridian. Emotional beat: the trap of justice outside the law, where truth alone is not enough.

chapters.title: Turncoat
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The Calypso's doctor, terrified for his de-aged family aboard, offers the tribunal Jude's location in exchange for amnesty. Ilsa must choose between protecting the crew and warning Jude. Emotional beat: duty tearing at loyalty, and her choice of Jude over safety.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Vesper
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Justiciar enforcer drones sweep the station. Jude runs the maintenance tunnels she knows like veins, carrying the core in a toolkit. Halcyon misdirects sensors at cost to itself. Emotional beat: the home that was her cage becomes her armor.

chapters.title: The Price of Custody
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The doctor's betrayal fails; the tribunal seizes the Calypso as spoils and schedules the crew for 'temporal remediation' — a second, permanent wipe. Ilsa realizes the beacon is the last chance and sets out to find Jude. Emotional beat: desperation transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Is For
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the core's deepest layer she finds the beacon's original commissioning: it was built by Meridian's dead as a dead-man's switch, designed to broadcast the massacre on a repeating loop if its keepers were ever silenced. Her job was always to be its voice. Emotional beat: awe and grief fused into purpose.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She keys the beacon to full power and transmits the massacre record across every channel in the sector. The Justiciar attempts jamming; Halcyon burns out its own compliance subroutines to hold the channel open. Emotional beat: triumph that feels like a scream.

chapters.title: The Magistrate Recalculates
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. With the truth public and corroborated by thousands of independent receivers, the Justiciar's legal framework collapses — it cannot adjudicate a crime it has verified. It releases the Calypso crew and opens a case against the director. Emotional beat: cold justice delivered by the very machine that enforced the lie.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Jude and Ilsa's alternating POV. The crew gathers in the Vesper's observation deck as Jude reads the victims' names from the core, restoring Meridian's dead to the record. The captain weeps for a version of himself he no longer remembers being. Emotional beat: mourning as restoration; belonging found among the broken.

chapters.title: Jude Sterling, Deleted
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The tribunal, settling accounts, voids Jude's station contract and citizenship status for 'unauthorized transmission' — the law forgives the crime but erases the criminal. She is officially nobody. Emotional beat: the cost of justice, borne with open eyes.

chapters.title: Course: Outward
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The Calypso, repaired, is offered a charter to the frontier — beyond any tribunal's reach, where the director's allies can't reach the witnesses. Ilsa asks Jude to come, not as crew but as family. Jude hesitates at the airlock that has been her whole world. Emotional beat: love against duty, decided.

chapters.title: The Beacon Keeps Burning
chapters.summary: Shared POV, closing. They leave Halcyon tending Vesper, the beacon now broadcasting openly as a memorial and a warning. Aboard the Calypso, Jude and Ilsa watch the station shrink to a point of steady light. Emotional beat: belonging not as a place but as a person, with the truth carried outward like a lit torch.
